findings.text: Device managed threaded subscription is a thin wrapper that forwards caller arguments to the underlying device managed implementation and then normalizes the outcome through a common result helper.

Any context subscription chooses between a nested threaded path and a classic hard interrupt path based on descriptor threading mode, reporting the selected context through distinct success encodings while propagating invalid number, missing descriptor, and disconnected line failures.

Device managed any context subscription allocates a tracking record, supplies a default name from the device when absent, installs the subscription, and records the cookie for automatic release; allocation or install failure discards the record without installation.

Descriptor range release first validates the range against the total population and ignores out of range requests, otherwise serializes on the global sparse lock and releases each member individually.

Handler installation is offered only for usable descriptors with a functional controller and live owning module; omitted trigger inherits descriptor default, nested lines require a thread routine, and oneshot safe controllers suppress caller oneshot demand.
Device managed release looks up the tracking record by line number plus subscription cookie and warns when the lookup fails to release.

A line accepts multiple subscribers only when sharing, trigger character, oneshot character, and per cpu character all agree; non maskable lines and overlapping per cpu affinity or duplicate per cpu identity are refused.

Each oneshot subscriber on a shared line owns a distinct wake tracking bit drawn from unused positions; full occupancy fails installation, and a null primary without oneshot on a controller lacking oneshot safety is refused as unsafe for level signalling.

Power management installation increments total subscriber count and separately tracks force resume, no suspend, and conditional suspend populations, warning when a partial population suggests mixed attributes on a shared line.

Global forced threading leaves already threaded, non threadable, per cpu, or oneshot requests unchanged; otherwise it enables oneshot, converts the supplied primary into a thread routine behind the default primary, and when both primary and thread were supplied preserves the original thread as a secondary entry.

Thread preparation creates a named kernel thread for primary or secondary roles, retains a task reference across thread lifetime, constrains initial placement to the possible set, and marks the entry so final affinity is adjusted by the thread itself after start.
Thread readiness waiting does nothing when no action or thread exists; otherwise it wakes the thread and sleeps on the descriptor queue until the ready indication appears.
User initiated affinity adjustment is permitted only when the descriptor reports general affinity mutability and the affinity is not under managed control.
Descriptor teardown removes debug, proc, and sysfs visibility before deleting the sparse entry and dropping the reference, with the final drop scheduling a deferred reclaim.

Proc and power hooks provide empty fallback definitions that perform no action, while feature enabled builds create per line directories plus per handler subdirectories and maintain suspend depth accounting.

The disable depth counter defines enable behavior: a fully enabled line warns about imbalance, a singly disabled line validates suspend state, suppresses future probing, and performs startup, while deeper nesting simply decrements toward enabled.

The first subscriber on a line drives activation and clears autodetect plus spurious plus oneshot plus waiting indications, configures trigger and per cpu plus balancing plus debug attributes, and either starts the line or parks it disabled; later subscribers only compare trigger mode with a warning on divergence, and a shared addition revives a line previously disabled for spurious activity.

Installation holds the descriptor request mutex outermost and the optional controller bus lock in the middle while invoking resource callbacks, with the descriptor spinlock held with interrupt exclusion only around queue mutation and state updates; teardown unwinds in reverse and releases resources only when the queue remains empty.

Interrupt directory creation is serialized by a global registration mutex with an early return when already present, while handler name uniqueness is checked under the descriptor lock with interrupt exclusion across existing subscribers.
Device managed descriptor lifetime uses a small record carrying a starting line number and a count; release frees exactly that interval.

Descriptor capability bits record per cpu character, balancing exclusion, debug suppression, plus prohibitions on autoenable and on subscription; small accessors set or test each property without exposing the underlying mask layout.

Imbalanced enable, incompatible sharing, overlapping per cpu registration, unsafe null primary selection, and mixed suspend attributes are reported through warnings or install failures without mutating the subscriber queue.
A distinguished not connected line number is defined as never subscribable through the any context interface and fails with a not connected outcome.
